messages:
Anya: Heads up — ECC correctable spike in pool-west-2, noticed ~50 cards with elevated counts, ~+120% over baseline in the last 30m. Not seeing clear XIDs yet.
Sam: Got the alert. Alarm timestamped ~1762342000. I saw auto-drain didn't run. Was that expected?
Ops-bot: ALERT: ECC_CORRECTABLE_SPIKE detected in pool-west-2 (50 cards), threshold=100/hr per-pool.
Harper: Auto-drain policy today only does soft-drain on correctables; hard drains require >=200/hr sustained 15m or presence of uncorrectable/XID.
Kevin: Before we change thresholds — what's the SLO/availability impact right now?
Sofia: Worked it up — tail latency (99.9) spiked ~8% across impacted hosts in same window. Jobs retried gracefully, so end-user error rate is low, but cost per request went up.
Anya: Proposal: run an experiment lowering soft-drain threshold to 80/hr per-card for a constrained cohort (10% traffic) in west-2a/b. Dry-run first (log only) then optional soft-evac.
Jen: +1 for experiment but gate by workload priority — only non-prod and background jobs should be eligible for automatic evacuations.
Sam: Agreed. Add tag evict-expt-v2 and limit to west-2a/b. Also create a dry-run flag so we can validate decision logic without requeues.
Harper: Update to runbook I suggest: ignore transient bursts shorter than 3m and require either sustained rate or correlated XID/unrecoverable patterns. Also check power-cycle and driver uptimes when correlating.
Anya: Draft config (pseudo):
```
# evac-expt-v2
scope: pool-west-2a,b
dry_run: true
percent_traffic: 10
soft_drain_threshold_per_card: 80/hr
burst_window: 3m
min_sustained_window: 10m
workload_filter: [non-prod, background]
```

Ops-bot: Scheduled experiment: start=2024-06-18T16:00Z, dry_run=true, scope=west-2a,b, percent=10. Reminder will be posted at start.
Kevin: One more safety net: if total drained cards in a pool would exceed 10% capacity, do an automatic regional fallback and page oncall rather than draining more. Keeps capacity intact.
Sofia: Cost tradeoff reminder — evictions cause requeues and a ~10% infra cost bump for that traffic. We should document that in the runbook and Slack announcement. :grimacing:
Sam: Fine with the plan for a dry-run. Requirement: create an observability dashboard with per-card timelines, histogram of ECC rates, and driver version breakdown before we move to active drains.
Jen: I'll own the dashboard. Need a new trace that joins NVML ECC counters, driver version, and host power events. ETA EOD tomorrow.
Anya: I'll run backtests against the last 6 months of spikes using the proposed thresholds and report the false-positive rate and potential cost impact by tomorrow morning.
Harper: I'll update the runbook draft under /docs/infra/ecc-evac-runbook.md (link) and add a checklist for experiment rollout + rollback criteria. Ping oncall if we observe >150 cards affected or if XIDs appear.
Sam: Thanks — if the dry-run looks good we can scale to 50% traffic and then evaluate global rollout. Keep this thread for results and logs.
